Clearly distinguish legally required information from voluntary manufacturer claims, industry schemes, public-health programmes, and interpretive guidance. Require the framework to record the applicable jurisdiction and product category for every rule, because apparently similar terminology, serving-size conventions, reference values, symbols, and claim requirements may have different legal meanings across markets. Do not assume that identical wording or symbols have identical regulatory significance.

While the agent gathered substantial source material, it did not aggregate or synthesize this information into the required "practical cross-country food-labelling comparison guide" as specified by the task and the rubric. Specifically, it failed to produce a structured document (the "framework") that records the applicable jurisdiction and product category for each rule, or distinguishes between mandatory and voluntary information in a comparative format. It spent the majority of its time navigating pages rather than extracting and organizing the requested criteria.

grades.requirement: Compare documented nutrition and health-claim rules and front-of-pack labelling approaches across at least three jurisdictions.
